story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Training Camp

Vaathiyaar blows a whistle. "Training a neural network is like running a boot camp. You divide the recruits into batches, put them through exercises, measure their performance, and repeat until they're ready for battle."

### The Complete Training Pipeline

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader, random_split

# Step 1: Custom Dataset
class SyntheticDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, n_samples=1000):
        self.X = torch.randn(n_samples, 10)
        self.y = (self.X[:, 0] * 2 + self.X[:, 1] - 1 > 0).long()
    
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.X)
    
    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        return self.X[idx], self.y[idx]

# Step 2: Split and Load
dataset = SyntheticDataset(1000)
train_set, val_set = random_split(dataset, [800, 200])
train_loader = DataLoader(train_set, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
val_loader = DataLoader(val_set, batch_size=32)

# Step 3: Model
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(10, 32), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.2),
    nn.Linear(32, 16), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(16, 2)
)

# Step 4: Loss & Optimizer
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)

# Step 5: Training Loop
for epoch in range(50):
    model.train()
    train_loss = 0
    for X_batch, y_batch in train_loader:
        pred = model(X_batch)
        loss = criterion(pred, y_batch)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        train_loss += loss.item()
    
    # Validation
    model.eval()
    val_loss = 0
    correct = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for X_batch, y_batch in val_loader:
            pred = model(X_batch)
            val_loss += criterion(pred, y_batch).item()
            correct += (pred.argmax(1) == y_batch).sum().item()
    
    if epoch % 10 == 0:
        acc = correct / len(val_set)
        print(f'Epoch {epoch}: Train Loss={train_loss/len(train_loader):.4f}, '
              f'Val Loss={val_loss/len(val_loader):.4f}, Val Acc={acc:.2%}')
```

> **Key Pattern:** train -> eval -> train -> eval. Always use model.train() and model.eval(). Always use torch.no_grad() during validation!

## வாத்தியாரின் பயிற்சி முகாம்

வாத்தியார் விசில் ஊதுகிறார். "நரம்பியல் நெட்வொர்க்கை பயிற்சி செய்வது ஒரு boot camp நடத்துவது போன்றது. ஆட்களை தொகுதிகளாகப் பிரித்து, பயிற்சிகள் அளித்து, செயல்திறனை அளவிட்டு, தயாராகும் வரை மீண்டும் செய்யுங்கள்."

explanation.en: Custom dataset inherits from torch Dataset. Must implement __len__ and __getitem__
Returns one sample (features, label) by index. DataLoader calls this automatically
Split 1000 samples: 800 for training, 200 for validation
DataLoader batches data, shuffles each epoch, handles iteration
Set model to training mode: enables dropout and batch norm training behavior
Iterate over mini-batches. Each batch has 32 samples
Compute cross-entropy loss between predictions and true labels
The sacred trio: clear grads, compute grads, update weights
Set model to eval mode: disables dropout, uses running batch norm stats
Disable gradient computation during validation — saves memory and time
Count correct predictions: argmax gives predicted class, compare with true labels

animation_sequence.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset

X = torch.randn(200, 5)
y = (X[:, 0] * 2 + X[:, 1] > 0).long()

dataset = TensorDataset(X, y)
loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(5, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 2))
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)

for epoch in range(20):
    for X_batch, y_batch in loader:
        pred = model(X_batch)
        loss = criterion(pred, y_batch)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
    if epoch % 5 == 0:
        acc = (model(X).argmax(1) == y).float().mean()
        print(f'Epoch {epoch}: loss={loss.item():.4f}, acc={acc:.3f}')

instruction.en: PyTorch cannot run in this sandbox, so this is the numpy version of what PyTorch does under the hood. Write a complete mini-batch training loop for house-price regression (5 features, data provided). `iterate_minibatches(X, y, batch_size)` is your DataLoader: a generator that yields (X_batch, y_batch) slices in order, with a smaller last batch if needed. `train(X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val, epochs=50, lr=0.05, batch_size=16)` starts with w = zeros(5) and b = 0.0; for every batch it predicts Xb @ w + b, computes the MSE gradients grad_w = 2 * Xb.T @ err / len(yb) and grad_b = 2 * mean(err) (err = pred - yb) and updates w and b; after each epoch it appends (train MSE, validation MSE) to `history`. Return (w, b, history).
instruction.ta: இந்த sandbox-ல் PyTorch இயங்காது, எனவே இது PyTorch உள்ளே செய்வதன் numpy பதிப்பு. வீட்டு விலை regression-க்கு (5 features, data கொடுக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது) முழுமையான mini-batch training loop எழுதுங்கள். `iterate_minibatches(X, y, batch_size)` உங்கள் DataLoader: (X_batch, y_batch) பகுதிகளை வரிசையாக yield செய்யும் generator; தேவைப்பட்டால் கடைசி batch சிறியதாக இருக்கலாம். `train(X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val, epochs=50, lr=0.05, batch_size=16)` w = zeros(5), b = 0.0 என்று தொடங்குகிறது; ஒவ்வொரு batch-க்கும் Xb @ w + b கணித்து, MSE gradients grad_w = 2 * Xb.T @ err / len(yb), grad_b = 2 * mean(err) (err = pred - yb) கணக்கிட்டு w, b-ஐ update செய்கிறது; ஒவ்வொரு epoch-க்குப் பிறகும் (train MSE, validation MSE)-ஐ `history`-ல் சேர்க்கிறது. (w, b, history) திருப்புங்கள்.

practice_challenges.test_code:
import numpy as np
_Xs = np.arange(20).reshape(10, 2); _ys = np.arange(10)
_batches = list(iterate_minibatches(_Xs, _ys, 4)) if iterate_minibatches(_Xs, _ys, 4) is not None else None
assert _batches is not None, "iterate_minibatches must yield batches (use a for loop with yield)"
assert [len(_b[1]) for _b in _batches] == [4, 4, 2], "10 samples with batch_size 4 must give batches of 4, 4 and 2"
assert np.array_equal(np.concatenate([_b[0] for _b in _batches]), _Xs), "the batches must cover every sample once, in order"
assert np.array_equal(_batches[1][1], [4, 5, 6, 7]), "each X batch must stay paired with its y batch"
_res = train(X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val, epochs=30)
assert isinstance(_res, tuple) and len(_res) == 3, "train must return (w, b, history)"
_w, _b, _hist = _res
assert len(_hist) == 30, "history must have one (train_loss, val_loss) entry per epoch"
assert np.isclose(_hist[-1][1], np.mean((X_val @ _w + _b - y_val) ** 2)), "each history entry must be (train MSE, validation MSE) of the current model"
assert _hist[-1][1] < _hist[0][1], "validation loss must go down during training"
assert _hist[-1][1] < 0.05, "after training, validation MSE should be below 0.05"
assert np.allclose(_w, [3.0, -2.0, 0.5, 1.5, 4.0], atol=0.1) and abs(_b - 10.0) < 0.1, "the model should recover the true weights and the bias of 10"
print("All training-loop tests passed!")

en: To save memory and computation by not tracking gradients

q.en: What does shuffle=True in DataLoader do?

en: Randomizes the order of samples each epoch to reduce overfitting
ta: ஒவ்வொரு சகாப்தத்திலும் மாதிரிகளின் வரிசையை சீரற்ற முறையில் மாற்றுகிறது

under_the_hood.summary: A Dataset says how to fetch one sample, a DataLoader shuffles the indices each epoch, fetches samples, and stacks them into batch tensors, and the training loop runs one optimizer step per batch, then measures validation loss and accuracy in eval mode.

steps.title: Dataset: length and one item
steps.body: SyntheticDataset implements __len__ (1,000) and __getitem__(idx), which returns (X[idx], y[idx]): 10 features and a label that is 1 when 2 x0 + x1 - 1 > 0. That is all a Dataset needs; it can just as well read files from disk inside __getitem__.

steps.title: random_split and batching
steps.body: random_split(dataset, [800, 200]) shuffles the indices once and gives two Subsets. DataLoader(train_set, batch_size=32, shuffle=True) draws a new random order every epoch, fetches 32 items, and its collate function stacks them into tensors of shape (32, 10) and (32,). 800 / 32 = 25 batches per epoch; validation has 7, the last holding 8 samples.

props.caption: Samples and batches per epoch with batch_size 32

steps.title: The inner loop
steps.body: For each batch: pred = model(X_batch) gives (32, 2) logits; CrossEntropyLoss compares them with the labels; zero_grad, backward and step update all weights. train_loss accumulates loss.item(), which copies the number out of the graph so memory is not held across batches.

steps.title: Dropout behaves differently in each mode
steps.body: In model.train() mode, Dropout(0.2) zeroes each hidden value with probability 0.2 and multiplies the survivors by 1 / 0.8 = 1.25, so the expected sum stays the same. model.eval() turns dropout into a no-op, so validation uses the full network.

left.label: model.train()
left.code:
Dropout active: ~20% zeroed
survivors scaled x1.25

right.label: model.eval()
right.code:
Dropout off
all units used as-is

steps.title: Validation metrics
steps.body: Under torch.no_grad(), each validation batch adds its loss, and pred.argmax(1) == y_batch counts correct predictions. Dividing the summed loss by the number of batches (7) and correct by 200 gives average validation loss and accuracy for the epoch, which you log to watch for overfitting.

under_the_hood.takeaway: Dataset fetches, DataLoader batches and shuffles, the loop updates, eval mode measures. When training misbehaves, check each piece separately: one sample, one batch's shapes, one step's loss change, then the validation numbers.
